items.title: Heavy rain brings relief as Johor haze readings remain moderate
items.summary: JOHOR BARU: Heavy rain across parts of Johor this evening brought some relief from the haze, with air quality readings at all eight monitoring stations remaining at moderate levels. As of this evening, Larkin recorded the highest Air Pollutant Index (API) reading at 96, followed by Tangkak (92), Pasir Gudang (88) and Batu Pahat (87). An API reading of between 51 and 100 is classified as moderate, while readings above 100 indicate unhealthy air quality.

items.title: Istana Negri Sembilan draws media attention amid royal crisis
items.summary: Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim, Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi and Negri Sembilan Menteri Besar Datuk Ismail Lasim are understood to be seeking an audience with the Yang di-Pertuan Besar of Negeri Sembilan, Tuanku Muhriz Tuanku Munawir, who is currently at the palace. The palace crisis in Negri Sembilan has been ongoing since April, when the Undang Yang Empat proclaimed the removal of Tuanku Muhriz as the Yang di-Pertuan Besar of Negri Sembilan. The Undang Yang Empat subsequently proclaimed Tunku Nadzaruddin Tuanku Jaafar as the 12th Yang di-Pertuan Besar of Negri Sembilan.

items.title: AfD predicts Merz's exit as German chancellor faces mounting pressure
items.summary: BERLIN: Germany's far-right AfD predicted Monday that Chancellor Friedrich Merz will be out of office before the end of the year, a day after his centre-right CDU party suffered two bruising state election defeats. At just 16 months in office, Merz has seen his approval ratings plummet while his party has suffered a string of state vote losses against the AfD, which also leads the nationwide polls. Merz admitted that his CDU had suffered a "disaster" in Mecklenburg-Western Pomerania.

items.title: Cops confirm arson at two 24-hour convenience stores in Kuching
items.summary: Kuching police chief ACP Alexson Naga Chabu said the incidents occurred between 7.05pm and 8.30pm. The fire was extinguished by Fire and Rescue Department (Bomba) personnel. Alexson said police are investigating both incidents under Section 436 of the Penal Code, for mischief by fire or explosive substance with intent to destroy.

items.title: DAP ministers, deputies staying in Cabinet at Loke's request
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The decision by DAP ministers and deputy ministers to remain in the Cabinet was made at the request of the party's secretary-general, Anthony Loke. A source said all DAP ministers and deputy ministers had initially wanted to follow Loke's move to offer their resignation. "However, the DAP central executive committee (CEC), particularly Loke, asked all the ministers and deputy ministers to remain in the government administration.

items.title: Man found dead in petrol station toilet near Tronoh
items.summary: IPOH, Sept 21 — A 39-year-old local man was found dead inside the toilet of a petrol station in Taman Tronoh Baru, near Tronoh, today. Perak Fire and Rescue Department (JBPM) Assistant Director of Operations Sabarodzi Nor Ahmad said they received an emergency call at 2:20pm before a team of personnel from the Batu Gajah Fire and Rescue Station (BBP) arrived at the scene at 2:34pm. “Upon arrival, the police and the Ministry of Health (MOH) were already at the scene and found a man lying unconscious, as well as stuck in the toilet door frame.

items.title: ‘Urgent and important’: Serikin border complex fast-tracked for 2027 completion, says minister
items.summary: Minister in the Prime Minister’s Department (Sabah and Sarawak) Datuk Mustapha Sakmud said the border security project under the National Security Council (MKN) was placed in the ‘urgent and important’ category for fast-track implementation. “This project is also among the matters discussed in the Malaysia Agreement 1963 (MA63) Implementation Action Meeting as well as the MA63 Technical Committee Council. “Do not consider projects involving national security as ordinary projects.

items.title: Heavy rain five times usual level triggered KL flash floods
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA: Flash floods in several parts of the federal capital yesterday were triggered by exceptionally heavy rainfall recorded in the Ampang and Lembah Keramat catchment areas. Kuala Lumpur Mayor Datuk Seri Fadlun Mak Ujud said the 155 millimetres (mm) of rainfall recorded yesterday was more than five times the usual 30 mm in the federal capital. "Observations showed that heavy to very heavy rain was recorded across the Klang Valley yesterday afternoon, particularly in the upstream catchment areas of Ampang, Klang Gates Dam and Lembah Keramat in Selangor.

items.title: Melaka lawmakers await 'whistle' for assembly dissolution
items.summary: MELAKA: The dissolution of the Melaka state legislative assembly is expected to take place this week, based on an earlier indication by Chief Minister Datuk Seri Ab Rauf Yusoh. Duyong assemblyman Datuk Mohd Noor Helmy Abdul Halem said the "two Fridays" referred to by the chief minister had already arrived. "If we go by the signal given by the Melaka chief minister about the two Fridays to go before the state assembly dissolution, those two Fridays have already passed.

items.title: Hannah Yeoh: Loke’s resignation offer was DAP CEC’s final decision, must be respected
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Sept 21 — DAP secretary-general Anthony Loke’s offer to resign as Transport Minister was the final decision of the party’s Central Executive Committee (CEC) and must be respected. DAP CEC deputy secretary-general Hannah Yeoh said the CEC meeting last Saturday also heard various proposals and views before the decision was made. “That was the CEC’s decision.

items.title: Beyond trade: Anwar’s fourth China visit targets AI, digital economy and skills
items.summary: SHANGHAI, Sept 21 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim’s visit to Shanghai and Hangzhou beginning Tuesday is aimed at deepening economic ties, advancing digital trade frameworks and highlighting the importance of technical talent development. “This is the prime minister’s fourth visit to China (since becoming prime minister in 2022). Anwar, who is also the finance minister, will be accompanied by Investment, Trade and Industry Minister Datuk Seri Johari Abdul Ghani, Transport Minister Anthony Loke and Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail.

items.title: Ensure polytechnic, community college grads secure jobs matching their skills - Zambry
items.summary: KOTA KINABALU: The employability rate of polytechnics and community colleges (PolyCC) should be viewed beyond mere percentage figures, ensuring graduates secure jobs that match their skills and offer quality career prospects and suitable income levels. Higher Education Minister Datuk Seri Dr Zambry Abdul Kadir reminded polytechnics and community colleges not to rest on their laurels despite their graduates recording employability rates exceeding 98 per cent last year. As such, Zambry said the Ministry of Higher Education has made "PolyCC as the TVET Pioneer" one of the thrusts of the country's higher education sector, reinforced by the Malaysia Higher Education Plan 2026-2035 and the Polytechnic and Community College Strategic Plan 2026-2035.

items.title: KL mayor: Sunday flash floods hit city after Ampang, Lembah Keramat record 155mm rainfall
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Sept 21 — Flash floods in several parts of the federal capital yesterday were triggered by exceptionally heavy rainfall recorded in the Ampang and Lembah Keramat catchment areas. Kuala Lumpur Mayor Datuk Seri Fadlun Mak Ujud said the 155 millimetres (mm) of rainfall recorded yesterday was more than five times the usual 30 mm in the federal capital. “Observations showed that heavy to very heavy rain was recorded across the Klang Valley yesterday afternoon, particularly in the upstream catchment areas of Ampang, Klang Gates Dam and Lembah Keramat in Selangor.

items.title: Malaysia condemns repeated incursions at Al-Aqsa Mosque compound
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA: Malaysia strongly condemns the repeated incursions by the Zionist regime into the Al-Aqsa Mosque compound as an extreme provocation that violates the sanctity of al-Haram al-Sharif. Minister in the Prime Minister's Department (Religious Affairs) Dr Zulkifli Hasan said Al-Aqsa Mosque, as the first kiblat and the third holiest site for Muslims, must be defended. The statement came after about 100 Israeli settlers reportedly entered the Al-Aqsa Mosque compound on Sunday under tight security by Israeli security forces, ahead of the Yom Kippur observance.

items.title: Najib's daughter Putri Norlisa joins CTOS board
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: CTOS Digital Bhd has appointed former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak's daughter Putri Norlisa Najib as an independent non-executive director. Putri Norlisa is the daughter of Najib and his former wife Tengku Puteri Zainah Tengku Eskandar. Putri Norlisa later co-founded Putri Norlisa Chair in 2015.

items.title: Former deputy rural development minister Yahya Lampong dies at 86
items.summary: KOTA KINABALU: Former deputy rural development minister and Kota Belud member of parliament Datuk Yahya Lampong died at KPJ Ampang Puteri Specialist Hospital in Kuala Lumpur around 6am. His death was confirmed by his son, Masley Yahya, in a Facebook post. Yahya served as the Kota Belud MP from 1982 to 1986 after winning the seat as an independent candidate in the 1982 General Election.

items.title: Selangor expands Kita Selangor Voucher eligibility, households earning RM8,000 or below now qualify
items.summary: SHAH ALAM, Sept 21 — The Selangor government has expanded the eligibility threshold for the Kita Selangor Voucher (BKS) to include households with a monthly income of RM8,000 or below. It initially prioritised vulnerable groups such as single mothers and heads of hardcore-poor households before extending eligibility to households earning RM5,000 or less. “The state government has further expanded the eligibility threshold to include households earning RM8,000 or less.

items.title: JPJ nets RM91.2m from ‘H’ series plates, confirms RM10.7m winning bid for ‘H 1’
items.summary: The next highest was H 9 at RM4,969,999, followed by H 3 at RM4,209,777, H 5 at RM4,007,777 and H 8 at RM4 million. H 6 went for RM3.38 million, H 2 for RM3.18 million and H 7 for RM3.1 million. H 4 fetched RM2,437,777 and H 11 RM1,557,777.

items.title: Janda Baik visitors advised to check with resorts after flash floods
items.summary: BENTONG: Visitors planning to travel to Janda Baik are advised to contact their respective resorts, chalets or homestays before making the journey following yesterday's flash floods in Kampung Janda Baik. A spokesman for the Janda Baik Resort Association said only four chalets and homestays operating along Sungai Cherangin were affected by the overflowing river, while the remaining premises were operating as usual. "Guests who have made bookings and plan to travel to Janda Baik are advised to contact their respective resorts, chalets or homestays.

items.title: Putrajaya condemns Al-Aqsa storming, warns provocations risk sparking wider global conflict
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Sept 21 — Malaysia strongly condemns the repeated incursions by the Zionist regime into the Al-Aqsa Mosque compound as an extreme provocation that violates the sanctity of al-Haram al-Sharif. Minister in the Prime Minister’s Department (Religious Affairs) Dr Zulkifli Hasan said Al-Aqsa Mosque, as the first qibla and the third holiest site for Muslims, must be defended. The statement came after about 100 Israeli settlers reportedly entered the Al-Aqsa Mosque compound on Sunday under tight security by Israeli security forces, ahead of the Yom Kippur observance.

items.title: Haze: Unhealthy air quality recorded in 17 areas as of 4pm
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: A total of 17 areas still recorded unhealthy Air Pollutant Index (API) readings as of 4pm today, with Kapit in Sarawak the worst hit with a reading of 172. Kuching (Sarawak) and Cheras (Kuala Lumpur) each recorded readings of 157, while Putrajaya and Nilai (Negri Sembilan) recorded 156. Meanwhile, 41 areas recorded moderate readings, while six areas recorded good readings.

items.title: 1MDB seeks Federal Court ruling, says Malaysia should hear fraud claims against UK law firm
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Sept 21 — 1Malaysia Development Berhad (1MDB) has filed an application seeking leave to appeal the appellate court’s ruling that the High Court lacked the jurisdiction to hear its lawsuit against a UK law firm. She also told Bernama that the Federal Court has fixed October 12 to hear the leave to appeal application. 1MDB has put forward 24 questions of law concerning jurisdiction and consolidation of its suit in seeking leave to appeal from the Federal Court.

items.title: 1MDB files leave to appeal ruling that High Court lacks jurisdiction to hear suit against UK law firm
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA: 1Malaysia Development Bhd (1MDB) has filed an application seeking leave to appeal the appellate court's ruling that the High Court lacked the jurisdiction to hear its lawsuit against a UK law firm. She also told Bernama that the Federal Court has fixed October 12 to hear the leave to appeal application. 1MDB has put forward 24 questions of law concerning jurisdiction and consolidation of its suit in seeking leave to appeal from the Federal Court.

items.title: Ex-sports ministry officer denied fair trial, High Court hears
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Former Youth and Sports Ministry finance division secretary Otman Arsahd was denied a fair trial due to serious misdirection by the Sessions Court in evaluating prosecution evidence, the High Court heard. He said the second Sessions Court judge had failed to fully evaluate the evidence before convicting Otman, 67, and sentencing him to 15 years in jail and fining him RM284.2 million in 2023. Rafique said 70 prosecution witnesses testified during the trial, but the second judge personally heard only SP64 to SP70.

items.title: Over 4,800 MRSM huffaz have entered professional fields to date - Asyraf
items.summary: Asyraf said the Ulul Albab Tamhidi or 'mini Ulul Albab' initiative, launched early last year, has now been expanded to all 50 MRSM campuses nationwide, in addition to the eight main MRSM Ulul Albab institutions. Meanwhile, MRSM Kuantan won the Malay Language category in the debate competition, defeating runners-up MRSM Pengkalan Hulu. In the Arabic Language category, MRSM Gemencheh emerged champions after defeating MRSM Tun Ahmad Abdullah Badawi, while MRSM Langkawi won the English Language category by defeating MRSM Tun Ghafar Baba.

items.title: ‘Possibly the most effective transport minister’: Lim Guan Eng praises Loke’s RM21b infrastructure legacy in Penang
items.summary: GEORGE TOWN, Sept 21 — DAP Air Putih assemblyman Lim Guan Eng said today that Transport Minister Anthony Loke’s impending departure from the federal Cabinet represents a major loss for Penang, crediting him with securing federal approval for more than RM21 billion in critical transport infrastructure for the state. In a press statement, the former Penang chief minister detailed the federal investments championed by Loke during his ministerial tenure. “With RM 21 billion of approved transportation projects in Penang, Loke is possibly the most effective transport minister who has done the most for Penang compared to the series of MCA transport ministers before him,” Lim said.

items.title: Motorcyclist killed in three-vehicle crash at Sultan Iskandar Highway tunnel
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: A 22-year-old motorcyclist was killed in a three-vehicle accident at Tunnel 2 of the Sultan Iskandar Highway heading towards Jalan Damansara here this morning. Kuala Lumpur Traffic Investigation and Enforcement Department chief Assistant Commissioner Mohd Zamzuri Mohd Isa said the victim was travelling in the right lane when he collided with the Honda City, which was in the same lane. He said the two other drivers involved — a 28-year-old man driving the Honda City and a 40-year-old lorry driver — were unhurt.

items.title: Malaysia-China ties set for further boost during Anwar's China visit
items.summary: SHANGHAI: Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim's working visit to this metropolitan city, starting tomorrow in conjunction with WorldSkills Shanghai 2026, is significant in maintaining the momentum of close ties between Malaysia and China. Malaysian Ambassador to China Datuk Norman Muhamad said the visit reflects the growing bilateral relations, particularly following several official visits by China's top leadership over the past three years. He said high-level exchanges during this period, involving the prime minister, deputy prime minister and the Yang di-Pertuan Agong, demonstrated the solid foundation of Malaysia-China ties.

items.title: Umno seeks release of Najib's frozen assets for RM50m fine [WATCH]
items.summary: PARIT: Umno hopes the courts will consider allowing a portion of former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak's frozen personal assets to be released to pay his RM50 million fine. Umno secretary-general Datuk Dr Asyraf Wajdi Dusuki said that the party is actively pursuing this effort. This was subject to Najib meeting certain conditions, including paying a RM50 million fine.

items.title: Former deputy minister Datuk Yahya Lampong dies at 86
items.summary: KOTA KINABALU, Sept 21 — Former deputy rural development minister Datuk Yahya Lampong, who also served as the Kota Belud Member of Parliament, died at the age of 86 at KPJ Ampang Puteri Specialist Hospital, Kuala Lumpur, at about 6am today. The death was confirmed by his son, Masley Yahya, in a Facebook post today, although the cause of death has yet to be confirmed. Yahya served as the Kota Belud MP from 1982 to 1986 after winning the seat as an independent candidate in the 1982 General Election.

items.title: Malaysian glove makers eye up to US$2.50 price hike in October
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysian glove makers plan to raise selling prices by US$2 to US$2.50 per carton in October to offset higher production costs, with another increase possible as early as November, according to RHB Research. The firm said its channel checks showed producers were preparing to raise prices after generic nitrile glove average selling prices (ASPs) fell to between US$19 and US$20 per 1,000 pieces in September, from a peak of US$27 to US$28 in May. He said China's Intco Medical had raised prices by 15 yuan (US$2.24) to 40 yuan (US$5.97) per carton from Sept 9, giving Malaysian manufacturers room to follow with their own increases in October.

items.title: Ten ex-Bar presidents urge federal intervention in Negri Sembilan dispute [WATCH]
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Ten former presidents of the Malaysian Bar have called on the federal government to step in and resolve the constitutional issues surrounding the position of the Yang Dipertuan Besar of Negri Sembilan, Tuanku Muhriz Tuanku Munawir. In a joint statement today, they described the recent developments involving Tuanku Muhriz as raising serious concerns over the constitutional monarchy and rule of law. They said the Negri Sembilan state executive council (exco) had purportedly removed Tuanku Muhriz without the process required under Article 10 of the Laws of the Constitution of Negri Sembilan (UUTKNS) 1959.

items.title: [UPDATED] Najib's home inspected as preparations for house arrest continue
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Police and Prisons Department officers have assessed Datuk Seri Najib Razak's residence in Jalan Langgak Duta as preparations continue for the former prime minister's conditional house arrest. Sentul police chief Assistant Commissioner Anuar Bakri Abdul Salam said officers from both agencies inspected the residence this afternoon, including necessary security arrangements should the house-arrest order be implemented. Under the proposed division of responsibilities, Anuar said the Prisons Department would be responsible for security inside the residence, while police would handle security outside.

items.title: Amanah wants Negri MB to seek state assembly dissolution
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Parti Amanah Negara (Amanah) wants Negri Sembilan Menteri Besar Datuk Ismail Lasim to seek the dissolution of the state legislative assembly amid the latest dispute between the state executive and the palace. Amanah secretary-general Muhammad Faiz Fadzil said the party took note of Yang di-Pertuan Besar Negri Sembilan Tuanku Muhriz Tuanku Munawir's decision to withdraw his consent and revoke the appointments of all 10 state executive councillors. "The party takes note that the political turmoil in Negri Sembilan has reached a very critical stage when the Yang di-Pertuan Besar has withdrawn his consent and revoked the appointments of all members of the Negri Sembilan state executive council who were appointed following the 16th Negri Sembilan state election for breaching their oath," he said in a statement today.

items.title: Court rules developer cannot turn common property into private assets
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA: The Court of Appeal has ruled that a property developer cannot turn areas meant for residents' common use into private property before selling them or using them as security for bank loans. The court upheld a High Court decision that 342 car park bays, seven basement areas, landscaped areas, rooftops, a reception area and external façade spaces were common property belonging to the development and should be managed by the PJ Centrestage Joint Management Body (JMB). Azizah, who wrote the grounds of judgment, said the disputed areas were common property under the Building and Common Property (Maintenance and Management) Act 2007 (BCPA).

items.title: South Korean soldiers among three injured in DMZ mine blast
items.summary: SEOUL: Three people, including South Korean soldiers, were injured in a suspected mine blast inside the Demilitarised Zone (DMZ), South Korea's Yonhap TV reported on Monday. Yonhap TV reported that three soldiers were injured in the incident, and were taken to the Armed Forces Capital Hospital. It was not yet clear whether the mine was planted by North Korean forces or belonged to the South Korean military, Yonhap TV said.

items.title: Malaysia’s air quality improves slightly, but Kapit and Serian remain shrouded in haze
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 21 — Air quality in Kapit, Sarawak, deteriorated steadily throughout the day, overtaking other hotspots to become the most polluted location in Malaysia as of 4pm today. Nationwide, a total of 17 monitoring stations remained in the “Unhealthy” bracket (API 101 to 200), down from the 21 affected stations reported earlier in the morning. Sarawak accounts for majority of affected areas Sarawak remained by far the hardest-hit state, accounting for 10 of the 17 unhealthy stations nationwide.

items.title: Iran warns US of new weapons, targets if attacks resume
items.summary: TEHERAN: Iran's Revolutionary Guards on Monday warned they would attack new targets and deploy new weapons if the US launches further attacks on the country. Almost seven months into their war, Teheran and Washington remain locked in a stalemate, though neither side appears willing to return to full-scale war. "We will introduce new weapons with new capabilities into the battlefield, and the world will be surprised," he said.

items.title: Sentul police chief, prisons officers at Najib's residence for house arrest preparations
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Sentul police chief Assistant Commissioner Anuar Bakri Abdul Salam and Prisons Department officers arrived at Datuk Seri Najib Razak's residence in Jalan Langgak Duta today amid preparations for the former prime minister's conditional house arrest. It is understood that a meeting involving police and Prisons Department officers was held this afternoon to discuss procedures and security arrangements for the house arrest. Anuar Bakri arrived at 2.20pm, followed by Prisons Department officers at 3.15pm.

items.title: Imran Khan's three sisters arrested as Pakistan opposition plans protest
items.summary: ISLAMABAD: Former Pakistan prime minister Imran Khan's party said on Monday that his three sisters had been arrested. "Punjab police have raided Aleem Khan's home and have abducted Imran Khan's other two sisters, his nephews and their children," Zulfi Bukhari, a spokesman for Khan's Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf (PTI) party, said on his social media platform X. The law enforcement agencies arrested Khan's sisters Aleema Khan, Dr Uzma Khan and Noreen Khan from Lahore, the capital city of Punjab province.

items.title: Two men from China fined RM4,700 each over crypto investment scam
items.summary: JOHOR BARU: Two men from China were fined RM4,700 each by the magistrate's court today after pleading guilty to conspiring to carry out a bogus online cryptocurrency investment scam earlier this month. Chen Le, 36, and Zhong Guoxuan, 31, pleaded guilty after the charge was read before magistrate Atifah Hazimah Wahab. The charge was read together with Section 34 of the Penal Code for common intention.

items.title: China confirms Xi to visit US this week for Trump talks
items.summary: BEIJING: China's leader Xi Jinping will visit the United States this week for talks with President Donald Trump, Beijing confirmed on Monday. Beijing would "work with the US to enrich the substance of the relationship of constructive strategic stability between China and the US, strengthen dialogue and cooperation, (and) properly manage differences", he added. The US leader was welcomed by China's vice president when he landed in Beijing for his state visit in May.

items.title: Deepavali Bazaar fees slashed 85pc, Hannah Yeoh sets RM400 cap in Brickfields
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Sept 21 — Participation fees for Kuala Lumpur’s 2026 Deepavali Bazaar have been cut by 85 per cent to a maximum of RM400, including the deposit, as part of efforts to reduce costs for traders. This year’s RM400 fee comprises a RM30 licence fee, RM150 service charge, RM150 site rental and RM70 deposit. In comparison, traders had to pay RM2,626 in 2025, comprising a RM21 licence fee, RM105 service charge, RM500 site rental and RM2,000 deposit.

items.title: Riverbank protection project brings relief to Kampung Pulau Pisang residents
items.summary: KOTA BARU: Residents of Kampung Pulau Pisang, who have endured severe riverbank erosion for years are breathing a sigh of relief following the implementation of a federal riverbank protection project. Kampung Pulau Pisang village head Zainab Deraman said the erosion worsened last December, with several stretches along the Kelantan River badly affected. Zainab said several houses had also been affected by the erosion, but residents received immediate assistance when necessary.

items.title: AG: Najib’s family hasn’t paid RM50m fine, house arrest still on hold
items.summary: KAJANG, Sept 21 — Former Prime Minister Datuk Seri Najib Tun Razak has yet to pay the RM50 million fine stipulated as a condition for serving the remainder of his prison sentence under house arrest. “As of now, Datuk Seri Najib’s family has not paid the fine. Najib, 73, has been serving his sentence at the Kajang Prison since Aug 23, 2022, following his conviction for misappropriating RM42 million belonging to SRC International Sdn Bhd.

items.title: Sabah electricity reserve margin rises to 19pc, expected 26pc by year‑end, says Hajiji
items.summary: “This is in line with the Sabah Energy Roadmap and Master Plan (SE-Ramp 2040) and the target of achieving a 50 per cent renewable energy capacity mix by 2035,” he said in a statement after chairing the Sabah Energy Council meeting at Menara Kinabalu here today. The Chief Minister said Sabah’s electricity supply system had shown significant improvement since the state took over regulatory control of electricity supply and renewable energy. Sabah assumed regulatory control of electricity supply and renewable energy following the approval of the Electricity Supply Enactment 2024, Sabah Renewable Energy Enactment 2024 and amendments to the Sabah Energy Commission Enactment 2023 by the State Legislative Assembly on Jan 3, 2024.

items.title: ‘Not true’, says Prisons Department as singer Yasin alleges ‘taiko’ bosses rule jail life
items.summary: KOTA BHARU, Sept 21 — The Malaysian Prisons Department has denied claims by singer-composer Yasin Sulaiman that life in prison depends on money and influence. Prisons Department senior director of prison policy Mohamad Rosidek Musa said the claim was untrue, as it has standard operating procedures (SOP) to handle misconduct or negative incidents among inmates. he told reporters after the closing ceremony of the Malaysian Prisons Department Bookathon Programme 2026 at Pengkalan Chepa Prison here today.

items.title: Ex‑farmers’ group manager faces 27 forged document charges in RM540,000 oil palm deals
items.summary: SHAH ALAM, Sept 21 — A former Area Farmers Organisation (PPK) marketing manager today claimed trial in the Sessions Court here to 27 charges of using forged documents involving oil palm purchases worth more than RM500,000. Airulnizam Island, 44, who held the position at Bernam Jaya PPK in Sabak Bernam made the plea after all 27 charges were read out before Sessions Court Judge Datuk Mohd Nasir Nordin. The offences were allegedly committed at Bernam Jaya, Lot PT 608, Simpang 4, Bagan Nakhoda Omar, Sabak Bernam.

items.title: Did someone just win a ‘H1’ plate with a RM10.7m bid? RTD keeps everyone guessing
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 21 — A bid of RM10.7 million for the coveted H1 vehicle registration number has raised eyebrows online after bidding for the special H series closed yesterday, although the Road Transport Department (RTD) has yet to confirm the figure. Before the H series, the highest confirmed the bid was RM1.75 million for FFF 1, won by King of Malaysia Sultan Ibrahim in June 2024 and the highest amount ever paid for a Malaysian vehicle registration number. An unconfirmed screenshot shows an online bid for the ‘H1’ vehicle plate for RM10.777 million, possibly a new record for the highest JPJ number plate bid in Malaysia.

items.title: Tengku Zafrul: Asean’s next integration stage could draw on Malaysia’s NIMP 2030 principles
items.summary: SINGAPORE, Sept 21 — Asean’s next stage of economic integration could draw on the principles underpinned by Malaysia’s New Industrial Master Plan (NIMP) 2030, said Malaysian Investment Development Authority (Mida) chairman Tengku Datuk Seri Zafrul Abdul Aziz. Tengku Zafrul noted that Asean sits strategically between the East and West, astride some of the world’s most important trading routes. “Asean received US$226 billion (US$1=RM4.08) in foreign direct investment in 2024, almost twice the level recorded in 2015.

items.title: Socso confirms Ipoh crash victims’ families entitled to pensions and funeral aid exceeding RM275,000
items.summary: IPOH, Sept 21 — The next of kin of two victims killed in a road crash on Jalan Jelapang-Ampang here on Saturday are eligible for benefits under the Social Security Organisation’s (Perkeso) Lindung 24 Jam Scheme for Non-Occupational Accidents. Perkeso said in a statement today that the victims were Muhammad Izdihar Rafiq Sarajil Korin and Muhamad Faiz Danial Jumri, both aged 19. According to Perkeso, the next of kin of Muhammad Izdihar are eligible for Dependants’ Benefit payments of RM945, distributed according to their respective shares, with his parents receiving the payments for life and his three siblings receiving them until they turn 21 or complete a degree.

items.title: Rauf: BN open to alliances for Melaka polls, but don’t negotiate on social media
items.summary: MELAKA, Sept 21 — Melaka Barisan Nasional (BN) chairman Datuk Seri Ab Rauf Yusoh has advised parties interested in collaborating with the coalition in the upcoming state election not to negotiate such matters via social media. Ab Rauf said BN remained open to negotiations with any party concerning the Melaka state election. In the last state election, BN, led by Ab Rauf, formed the state government after winning 21 of the 28 State Legislative Assembly seats.

items.title: Kulim man charged with murder after allegedly killing wife in fit of jealousy
items.summary: KULIM, Sept 21 — A former technician was charged in the Magistrate’s Court here today with murdering his wife at their home in Taman Tiram last week. He was charged with murdering S. Sila, 39, at a house in Taman Tiram here between 6.30 pm and 9.04 pm on Sept 14. The court fixed Dec 8 for mention.

items.title: Negeri Sembilan MB says Yamtuan can’t dismiss excos without his advice, insists current line-up still valid
items.summary: KUALA LUMPURT, Sept 21 — Negeri Sembilan Menteri Besar Datuk Ismail Lasim said today that the state's executive councillors remain in office, arguing that the Yang di-Pertuan Besar cannot remove them without his advice. In a statement a day after the palace announced it had revoked all exco appointments, Ismail said the state's administrative system rests on constitutional monarchy and parliamentary democracy. Ismail also said Article 38(5), which deals with the tenure of exco members, cannot be read on its own.

items.title: Ex‑TH Properties deputy GM pleads not guilty to abetting RM14,000 CBT case
items.summary: KOTA BHARU, Sept 21 — A former TH Properties deputy general manager of construction projects pleaded not guilty in the Sessions Court here today to abetting a criminal breach of trust involving RM14,000 in penalty funds collected from a contractor for a commercial building project owned by Tabung Haji (TH). Tengku Kamarolhisham Tengku Kamaruddin, 55, is charged with abetting Mohamad Hashim Mukhatap, then a construction manager at THP Timur Sdn Bhd and an agent entrusted with the funds. The money was allegedly connected to penalties collected from contractor Kelpile Sdn Bhd for a proposed Tabung Haji-owned commercial development on Lot 273, Section 12, Bandar Kota Bharu, Kelantan.

items.title: Police: Preliminary probe finds Ipoh motorcyclists speeding in convoy before fatal crash
items.summary: TANJONG MALIM, Sept 21 — Police said preliminary investigations found that the group of motorcyclists involved in the accident along Jalan Jelapang-Ampang, Ipoh, which claimed three lives last Saturday, were believed to have been travelling at high speed while riding in a convoy. Perak police chief Datuk Mohd Alwi Zainal Abidin said investigations also found that some members of the group travelling from Ipoh subsequently lost control and crashed into a Toyota Vios. However, he said after police completed their operations at around 3am, the motorcyclists would return to gather and resume the activities.

items.title: Amirudin: PH Plus in Melaka more electoral pact than coalition given short preparation window
items.summary: ALOR GAJAH, Sept 21 — Pakatan Harapan (PH) views the PH Plus cooperation for the Melaka state election as more suitable as an electoral understanding rather than a new political coalition, given the increasingly limited time for preparations. PH election director Datuk Seri Amirudin Shari said the time available was currently too short to form a new coalition, but an understanding for electoral purposes could still be reached. More towards an electoral understanding.

items.title: Lubok Antu and Kanowit schools close as haze pushes API past 200
items.summary: The Sarawak Education Department (JPNS) said the decision was made based on Air Pollutant Index (API) readings recorded in the two areas as of 9am today. According to the Natural Resources and Environment Board’s API Status for Sarawak, Kanowit and Lubok Antu had recorded ‘very unhealthy’ API readings of 212 and 207 as of 10am. It also said that for schools located near districts recording API readings above 200, headmasters and principals may consider implementing PdPR, taking into account the health and safety of pupils.

items.title: PM Anwar appeals for unity, tells parties to stop playing racial card when desperate
items.summary: MELAKA, Sept 21 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has once again cautioned political parties against exploiting racial issues to gain public support. He said such tactics are often deployed when political parties find themselves in desperate situations, particularly during political dynamics that work against them. As the nation approaches nearly 70 years of independence, Anwar said Malaysia must emerge as a nation that thrives on the collective strength of its diverse races, regardless of who leads the country.

items.title: Two Negeri Sembilan excos confirm getting palace dismissal letter
items.summary: SEREMBAN, Sept 21 — Negeri Sembilan State Executive Councillor Suhaimizan Bizar has confirmed receiving a formal letter revoking his appointment with immediate effect last night. Bernama reported separately that State Entrepreneurship, Human Resources, Climate Change, Cooperatives and Consumerism Committee chairman Fairuz also confirmed receiving his dismissal letter from the state palace. Efforts to contact other affected state executive councillors to ascertain further developments were unsuccessful.
